title: the control that never ran, and the promise nobody verified
intent: The nine findings were checked before being fixed, and the check found two more. The first is a hole in the law the method rests on: a control that DID NOT RUN was read as a control that failed, so a claim whose control had a typo in it read as PROVEN - the method certified a check it had never seen fail. The second is the coverage number hiding unchecked promises: three never-checked claims over a three-file tree gave uncovered: 0, and the tree looked fully covered while nothing in it had been checked.
objection: Both fixes make the method say no more often, and the method's own map already cannot be green: a judgment in the set keeps the verdict unknown for ever. A method that refuses more and more often, on its own repository, is a method that has become a brake - and the law of the brake is that it is right about the brakes and wrong about the engine.
refuted_by: The agent arm, repeated with this build: if the protocol arm's map sends the agent to work that is not the work, the arm will show it - by taking longer on the same task, or by declaring promises that do not hold. Until that arm runs, the two fixes rest on the method's own judgement about itself.
